items.title: US military vs Iran's 'arch defence': Dangerous new phase of war looms
items.description: While Donald Trump talks about ending and winning the war in Iran, major US military assets are still on their way to the Middle East. These are the options they give him.

items.title: Iran 'holding global economy hostage' as Australia joins urgent Hormuz talks
items.description: Military planners are set to meet after ministers from 40 countries, including Australia's Penny Wong, attended virtual talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Asian fuel suppliers are restricting exports and it could hurt Australia
items.description: Australia imports most of its jet fuel from Asia, particularly China, Singapore and South Korea. But those countries rely on the Middle East for crude oil, meaning they are particularly vulnerable to the impacts of war.

items.title: Are we there yet? Why fuel prices could go much higher
items.description: Trying to guess exactly where the oil price tops out is fast becoming the chocolate wheel of choice among politicians, economists and oil experts.

items.title: What the shifting language of Australia's leaders reveals about the Iran war
items.description: With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, world oil markets rattled and no obvious off-ramp to the hostilities in sight, the major parties have dialled back their initial optimism.

items.title: US Attorney-General Pam Bondi sacked by Donald Trump
items.description: The US president had been growing increasingly frustrated with Pam Bondi's performance especially over her handling of the Epstein files, according to US media.

items.title: 'Extremely rare': April comets may put on a show for sky watchers
items.description: Two comets are currently hurtling towards the Sun. If they survive the trip, they may put on a dazzling show for Australian stargazers this month.

items.title: Four or more drinks may triple liver damage risk for many adults
items.description: Heavy drinking on the occasional Saturday night — even if you don't drink at all for the rest of the month — may damage your liver more than previously understood.

items.title: 'Rubber time', bottoms up and reading the silence: What's doing business like in Asia?
items.description: In Australia, a good deal builds relationships. In Asia, the opposite is often true. Here are some other cultural differences to understand.

items.title: How the ripple effects of the fuel crisis are hurting small-town Australians
items.description: In one community, the effects of the fuel crisis are not always where you would think.

items.title: Trump's speech was significant for what he did not say
items.description: The US president's national address was largely a cobble-together of past talking points and Truth Social posts. Perhaps the most notable takeaways relate to what went unmentioned.

items.title: Matildas players join Japan criticising 'inequality' in prize money
items.description: Fierce rivals on the field, the Matildas and Japan have joined forces to slam the Asian Football Confederation's prize money for the Women's Asian Cup.

items.title: Sea Eagles smash 'putrid' Dolphins in Foran's first game as coach
items.description: Kieran Foran gets off to a winning start on his NRL coaching debut as winless Manly Sea Eagles thrash the Dolphins in Redcliffe.

items.title: Premiership stars on song as Brisbane dominates Collingwood sans Daicos
items.description: Brisbane sends a timely reminder of its class to the rest of the competition as it easily dispatches Collingwood on Easter Thursday, as the Pies suffer without the injured Nick Daicos.

items.title: A New York Times critic used AI to write a review. This is why it matters
items.description: An author and freelance journalist has admitted to using AI to help him write a book review for the New York Times.

items.title: Cate Blanchett on why her life is 'barely controlled chaos'
items.description: The complexities of family light up Jim Jarmusch’s Golden Lion-winner, Father Mother Sister Brother, which features Blanchett alongside Adam Driver and Tom Waits.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A lost penguin, successful NASA rocket launch and address to the nation

items.title: Sit back and let us take you on a journey to the Moon with Artemis II
items.description: If all goes well for NASA's mission, the astronauts aboard could fly the furthest that humans have ever gone. What should we be looking out for?

items.title: In pictures: Artemis II NASA's first mission to the Moon in decades
items.description: For the first time in more than 50 years NASA has sent astronauts around the Moon, marking a major milestone in a new era of space exploration.

items.title: Grace heard a 'crack' at training the third time she injured her ACL
items.description: Australia has one of the highest rates of ACL injuries per number of people in the world, and younger people have the highest chance of tearing the ligament.

items.title: Sandra complained about her COVID vaccine injury, she says Services Australia then threatened her
items.description: For years these vaccine-injured Australians have been trying to get compensation from a 'torturous' government compensation scheme.

items.title: Iranian Nobel laureate suffers suspected heart attack in prison, family says
items.description: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi has been repeatedly charged and imprisoned by the regime over the past 25 years.

items.title: My kid wants to run with me. When can they start?
items.description: If you enjoy running and your child has shown interest in coming along, you might be wondering when they're old enough to start. Experts say there are a few ways you can determine if they're ready.

items.title: Travellers 'take the plunge' with cheap flights via Middle East despite warnings

items.title: Albanese's Scott Morrison moment came this week
